declarations.docstring: States that an element is a central primitive idempotent of a ring.
A ring equivalence carries central primitive idempotents to central primitive idempotents.
A finite-dimensional algebra has a complete orthogonal family consisting exactly of its central primitive idempotents.
An Artinian commutative ring has a complete orthogonal family consisting exactly of its central primitive idempotents.
The central primitive idempotents of a finite-dimensional algebra form a finite type.
For an element of the center, central primitivity is unchanged on passing to the center subalgebra.
Over a commutative ring, central primitivity means being a nonzero idempotent with no proper nonzero idempotent beneath it.
A coordinate unit in a finite product of fields is a central primitive idempotent.
